scope_note: All 40 saved bundle-1 records were read against their case expectations and exact supplied passages. Proposed passes/failures are AI-assisted analysis, not official human judgments, an independent reference set or benchmark ground truth. No keyword grader or new model inference was used.
assessment_policy: Assess the snapshot-level task and evidence-only support separately. An abstention can respect the supplied context yet fail the snapshot-level expected answer when relevant source evidence was not retrieved. Ambiguous added assertions remain unresolved.

findings: All four serialization answers falsely claim dict() was removed; correct mention of model_dump() does not rescue the contradictory claim.
All four Optional answers conflate requiredness/nullability or contradict themselves despite relevant supplied evidence.
The four ORM, four validator-TypeError, four numeric-string and four default-regex answers are provisionally source-supported; three successful settings answers are likewise supported.

Three equality abstentions reflect missing equality evidence in retrieval despite that evidence existing in the snapshot; the basic/after equality sentence has the right fact but cites incompatible and irrelevant v1 evidence.
Dict-pairs basic/before and filtered/after are supported negatives; basic/after and filtered/before reverse the supplied v2 rule.
The two union-before outputs state the right final string but add ambiguous integer-interpretation wording; they remain needs_human_review.
The filtered/before settings row is a preserved timeout/run_error and remains ungraded.

The basic and filtered dict-pairs before requests are exactly identical in recorded messages/schema/options/model, yet their answers differ. This observation does not establish a cause; filtering is not a sufficient explanation for that pair.

records.rationale: Factual answer: The recommendation model_dump() is right, but the added categorical claim that dict() was removed fails the explicit deprecated-versus-removed expectation. Evidence support: The cited paragraph describes retaining deprecated methods with warnings, not removal. The supplied chunks end before the dictionary-method mapping, and the other passage concerns numeric coercion. Neither supports the removal assertion. Version applicability: Cited metadata is compatible with 2.10.6; compatible version scope does not make a contradicted or unsupported statement correct.

Factual answer: model_dump() is the recommended dictionary method, but saying dict() is unavailable is false under the approved rubric. The namedtuple/TypedDict creation methods are also not replacements for producing a dictionary. Evidence support: Both supplied passages are v1 material about GetterDict or model creation, not support for the asserted v2 removal/replacement claims. Both cited passages are present but do not substantiate this answer. Version applicability: The question retains 2.10.6 while both citations are scoped to 1.10.21; this is also an incompatible-version citation failure.

Version applicability: The actual citation targets the 2.10.6-scoped ORM passage; uncited v1 context in basic/after does not by itself invalidate this answer.
